hints: Focus on what an increase in pH means, it means the solution becomes more alkaline, so look for a basic oxide.
Recall the trend across Period 3, oxides change from basic on the left to acidic on the right.
Check which of the four oxides reacts with water to release hydroxide ions, while the others are insoluble or form acids.
walkthrough:
**What does higher pH mean?**

Pure water has pH 7. An increase in pH means $\text{OH}^-$ ions are produced, so we need a basic oxide that forms an alkali in water.

**Apply the Period 3 oxide trend**

From left to right: $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{MgO}$ are basic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric and insoluble, $\text{SiO}_2$ is weakly acidic and insoluble, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ and $\text{SO}_2$ are acidic.

Key reaction for a basic oxide:
$$\text{MgO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2$$

**Pick the alkaline result**

$\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ releases $\text{OH}^-$ ions, so pH rises above 7. The other oxides either do not react with water or form acidic solutions, so only magnesium oxide fits.

options.A: MgO is a basic oxide. It reacts sparingly with water to form magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)2, which releases OH- ions and raises the pH above 7.
options.B: Al2O3 is amphoteric but essentially insoluble in water. It does not react with water to change the pH, a common trap is thinking amphoteric means it will make water alkaline.
options.C: SiO2 is acidic in character but is insoluble and does not react with water. It causes no pH change, students sometimes confuse it with its reaction with hot concentrated alkali.
options.D: SO2 is an acidic non-metal oxide. It dissolves to form sulfurous acid, H2SO3, which releases H+ ions and lowers pH, the opposite of what is asked: $$\text{SO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$$
